correctness.rationale: On five vertices the monomial exact sequence gives |Aut(E)|<=|D(Gamma)|*|Aut(Gamma)|. The standalone program enumerates all 2^25 directed graph masks, modulo all 120 vertex permutations; 291968 unlabeled graphs, 199957 with a cycle cover; for each checks all possible cover cycles, all root assignments in integer congruence arithmetic, and all graph automorphisms. The only graph achieving product 155 is the directed 5-cycle; only one other graph achieves product 126, the disjoint union of cycles of lengths 2 and 3; all remaining graphs have product at most 120. The five- and (two-plus-three)-cycle algebras achieve the bounds; coefficients normalize to 1 over C. Standalone checker produces VERIFY_OK, independent Hermite normal-form checks of diagonal group orders on 305 samples and Burnside orbit count produce CROSSCHECK_OK. Finite enumeration is exhaustive, not extrapolated to other n.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 survey identifies this as the first dimension above its verified small-size results in a conjecture for all perfect evolution algebras and simple examples. Establishing a uniform bound with a sharp 126 gap and uniqueness in this entire first open dimension closes a motivated concrete structural case, rather than an arbitrary parameter choice or known-table recalculation. The new integer-checkable certificate illuminates tradeoffs of diagonal and graph symmetry.
